Subject: Derivative training restriction & evidence request

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Greenbridge is interested in Redwood but we have two gating items from our privacy and procurement teams before we can move to contract: 1) a contractual commitment that REDWOOD will not use any Greenbridge prompts/responses for model improvement (i.e. no-derivative/no-training) for data we mark as "PHI" or "Confidential"; and 2) a short evidence package we can review showing how you will operationalize that commitment (logs, retention policy, routing to onshore hosts, or an export that proves exclusion).

Attached is our current DPA (DPA_Greenbridge_v1.2.pdf) — procurement has highlighted the training clause and would like to see proposed redlines. Can your legal/privacy/ops teams propose both: (a) proposed contract language and (b) an ops-level description (and sample logs) that would satisfy our auditors?

We expect to align with legal this week if feasible. Oliver from procurement is cc'd.

Best,
Samantha Lee

Samantha — thank you, and appreciate the attachment. I reviewed the DPA and have a focused proposal below. I attached a plain-text extract of the clause for quick copy/paste (proposed_DPA_clause.txt).

Proposed contractual approach (summary):
- Add a Training Exclusion clause: Redwood will not use Customer Data (defined to include prompts and generated responses) that is explicitly designated by the Customer as "Excluded Data" for the purpose of model improvement, derivative model training, or algorithmic refinement.
- Definition of Excluded Data: include tenant-level flags, and data labeled via metadata tags (we propose labels: PHI, Confidential) and a documented API parameter (no_train=true).
- Auditability: Redwood will provide an evidence package on request consisting of (i) a redacted sample of request logs showing exclusion flags, (ii) a description of retention settings (default 30d for excluded logs unless otherwise agreed), and (iii) routing proof if onshore processing is elected.
- Limited carveouts: for security and abuse detection, Redwood may process telemetry for malicious activity, provided that such processing does not feed model improvement pipelines and is retained only to the extent required by law.

Operational controls (ops summary for auditors):
- Runtime opt-out: per-tenant toggle + per-request no_train parameter. Requests with no_train or tenant opt-out are marked in the request metadata and filtered from offline model training jobs and from the streaming store used by training pipelines.
- KV/Prefix isolation: when customers elect onshore processing we keep separated storage paths and distinct ingestion queues that are not consumed by shared training jobs.
- Retention: by default excluded request logs and KV snapshots are retained 30 days; customers can request shorter retention or deletion.
- Evidence package: sample logs (redacted), export manifest, and a short configuration snapshot exported from our control plane.

Please let us know if Greenbridge prefers stronger retention language (e.g., max 14 days) or onshore KMS-only key control; we can propose specific language.

Would you like us to provide a small "ops proof pack" (redacted log extract + control-plane snapshot) to your auditors? If yes, share an email for secure upload or an SFTP endpoint.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Alex — this is helpful, thanks. A few clarifications from Greenbridge privacy & procurement: 

- Scope: we want all interactive chat sessions, embeddings created from patient text uploads, and API ingestion paths used by clinicians to be excluded when tagged PHI. (That should cover the main surface.)
- Retention: 14 days preferred for excluded logs; 30 days acceptable only with contractual cap.
- Evidence: we do want the ops proof pack. Please redacted-sample the request log showing the no_train flag and include a control-plane snapshot that shows the tenant opt-out toggle.
- KMS: we want the option to have onshore KMS for keys used to encrypt excluded data. If you offer that as a paid add-on, please include pricing guidance.

Attached: data_flow_diagram.png (shows our data ingress). Procurement would like the DPA redline tracked in DocuSign if possible.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee

Samantha — thanks, and glad the proposal is directionally aligned. A few concrete commitments we can make immediately for GBH (to be reflected in the DPA redline):

1) Contract language: we will add the Training Exclusion clause as Marissa proposed, with a defined retention cap of 30 days by default and an option for 14 days when explicitly elected in the contract.
2) Ops proof pack: Redwood will produce a redacted sample (single-day extract) showing the no_train flag present in request metadata plus a control-plane JSON snapshot demonstrating the tenant-level opt-out toggle. We will deliver the pack via a secure SFTP or signed DocuSign secure upload link.
3) KMS/onshore: We offer onshore KMS and onshore routing as a Dedicated add-on. Pricing for onshore KMS is included in an appendix; I'll have billing provide a ballpark in the next email.

Next steps: Marissa will prepare the tracked redline (DocuSign link attached in HubSpot) and I will coordinate the ops pack production. Can Greenbridge confirm a preferred retention cap (14 or 30 days) and an SFTP endpoint or secure inbox for the ops pack?

HubSpot: GBH-2027-045. DocuSign draft link: https://www.docusign.com/embedded-sign/ABC123-GREENBRIDGE-DPA

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
